raw_response:
I farm only 5 mu, so every bag of fertilizer costs me real money, but if yield falls, that hurts more. I do not like to change too much. I start from what we have done around here in recent years and make small adjustments. In Quzhou, with well water, wheat and maize can both give a decent harvest if I do the water and fertilizer on time. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put the base fertilizer down before sowing, then topdress nitrogen when it turns green in spring. Wheat here cannot be careless with water, so I will water after sowing if the ground is dry, then again at greening and booting. For maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed. Hybrids cost more, but I have seen many people around me get better ears and more grain with them, so I will follow that. I will not go too light on fertilizer. I would rather spend a bit more than watch the leaves turn pale and lose yield. On my small place, my wife and I can still manage most of the work ourselves, so I will keep the system simple: wheat with rotary tillage after maize, then maize with rotary tillage after wheat, timely irrigation from the well, and a couple of pesticide sprays each season when pests or disease show up.
